title: Prag Mahal - The Gothic Wonder of Bhuj
content:
Prag Mahal, Bhuj

Standing tall beside the famous Aina Mahal, Prag Mahal in Bhuj is a stunning example of 19th-century Gothic architecture. This majestic palace showcases a remarkable blend of European design and Indian craftsmanship, making it one of the most unique royal structures in Gujarat. With its towering clock tower, grand arches, and intricate carvings, Prag Mahal offers a glimpse into the royal grandeur of the Kutch rulers.

History of Prag Mahal

Prag Mahal was commissioned by Maharaja Pragmalji II in 1865 and designed by the renowned British architect Colonel Henry Saint Clair Wilkins. The construction was completed under the supervision of local artisans using Italian marble and sandstone from Rajasthan. The palace was built at a cost of 20 lakh rupees, a huge amount at that time, and remains a symbol of the royal family’s prosperity and artistic vision.
Although parts of it were damaged in the 2001 Bhuj earthquake, Prag Mahal still retains its historical charm and has been partially restored for visitors.

Architectural Highlights

  • Italian Gothic Design: The palace is built in the Italian Gothic style, featuring high arches, intricate jharokhas, and detailed stone carvings.
  • Clock Tower: The 45-meter-high clock tower offers a panoramic view of Bhuj city - a must-see for every visitor.
  • Darbar Hall: The grand hall displays royal portraits, hunting trophies, and antique furniture that tell stories of a glorious era.
  • Red Sandstone Walls: The palace’s striking red color comes from Rajasthan sandstone, which contrasts beautifully with the blue Bhuj sky.

Inside the Palace

Visitors can explore the main hall, corridors, and balconies, which still display fragments of the palace’s former splendor. The partially ruined yet magnificent setting has even attracted several Bollywood filmmakers - including the makers of Lagaan and Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam.

Timings and Entry Fee

  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM - 6:00 PM
  • Closed on: Thursdays and public holidays
  • Entry Fee: ₹20 for Indian visitors and ₹100 for foreign visitors

(Timings and fees may vary, so it’s advisable to confirm locally.)

Nearby Attractions

  • Aina Mahal: Located right next to Prag Mahal, this 18th-century palace is known for its dazzling mirror work and Indo-European style. Read more..
  • Hamirsar Lake: A scenic lake in the heart of Bhuj, perfect for evening walks and photography. Read more..
  • Kutch Museum: The oldest museum in Gujarat, showcasing local culture, weapons, and embroidery. Read more..
  • Bhujodi Village: A textile hub where local artisans weave beautiful handlooms and traditional fabrics. Read more..

How to Reach Prag Mahal

  • Nearest Airport: Bhuj Airport (around 5 km away)
  • Nearest Railway Station: Bhuj Railway Station (3 km away)
  • By Road: The palace is easily reachable by car, rickshaw, or local bus from anywhere in Bhuj.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Prag Mahal is from October to February, when the weather in Bhuj is cool and comfortable for exploring heritage sites.

faqs.question: Is Prag Mahal open to tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, it’s open as a heritage site and museum, except on Thursdays and public holidays.

faqs.answer: October to February is ideal for sightseeing in Bhuj due to pleasant weather.
